source: ASPIRE / MAFF -- Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique (BookID 251, 2018)
text:
Climate change is shifting rainfall timing and increasing pest/disease pressure, irregular rainfall, drought, and flooding, all of which can reduce rice yield and farmer income. Choosing the right variety and using water-management techniques suited to unpredictable rainfall can meaningfully reduce this risk.

Variety choice for uncertain rainfall: rice varieties fall into two groups by season sensitivity. 'Non-season-specific' varieties (e.g. Sen Pidao, Chulsar, IR66) can be planted in either the dry or wet season with little change in growth duration, making them more flexible when rainfall timing is uncertain. 'Season-specific' varieties (medium and heavy-duration types) can only be planted once per year, typically April to July, harvested mid-November to late January or February -- these are riskier if rains start late or end early. Short-duration varieties mature in 90-100 days in the dry season or 100-110 days in the wet season, which also reduces exposure to a full season of unpredictable weather.

Planting method matters for rainfall risk: for broadcast rice with irrigation access, seed is pre-sprouted (soaked, drained, left to sprout 1 day/night) then broadcast onto moist soil, with the field flooded about 7 days after sowing to help roots establish -- use roughly 80 kg/ha of seed for wet-season broadcast rice, or 120 kg/ha for short-duration broadcast rice. For rainfed dry-broadcast (no irrigation, fully dependent on rainfall), seed is broadcast dry directly onto prepared soil, sun-dried 1-2 hours before planting, and will germinate well once rain arrives -- even after a long dry spell, since the seed remains viable in the soil. This method uses less seed (60-80 kg/ha) with a mechanical seed drill.

Water management for irregular rainfall: broadcast rice germinates well within 3-5 days if soil moisture is adequate. Maintain a water depth of 3-5 cm at 7-10 days old, increasing to 20 cm for short-duration rice or 30 cm for medium/heavy rice from tillering through to maturity. If rainfall is insufficient or a dry spell occurs, supplement with irrigation to keep the soil moist rather than letting it dry out. In areas where rainfall is especially unpredictable and fields dry quickly: maintain strong field bunds to retain water without over-flooding during the growing stage, keep the field well-weeded, and where possible dig a small reservoir pond (roughly 20m x 10m) within the field to store a water reserve for dry spells during the wet season. Small drainage channels around the field edge also help release excess water if rainfall is unusually heavy.
